reason: E3 directly supports the formation of micro-galvanic cells at phase boundaries and accelerated dissolution, but the cited evidence does not demonstrate that mechanical wear is the trigger for exposing these boundaries, nor does it show the proposed feedback cycle between corrosion and wear. E1 and E2 discuss wear and oxidation separately but do not link them to the claimed mechanism.
premises: Wear exposes phase boundaries between electrochemically dissimilar phases in the HEA.
Exposed phase boundaries create micro-galvanic cells due to potential differences.
Micro-galvanic cells accelerate anodic dissolution of the more active phase.
Localized corrosion undermines structural integrity, enhancing mechanical wear.
This cycle accelerates overall degradation at elevated temperature.
